public_sources.title: Wang & Ramdas, Anytime-valid t-tests and confidence sequences for Gaussian means with unknown variance
public_sources.use: Shifted scale-invariant Gaussian t-test martingale and fixed-time factor; the factor distribution depends on standardized location relative to nuisance scale and the paper gives the exact G_n^(c,mu0) form.

public_sources.title: Wasserman, Ramdas & Balakrishnan, Universal Inference
public_sources.use: Finite-sample likelihood-ratio inference against composite nulls and sequential/profile-likelihood extension; used as the conceptual basis for the frozen-confidence-set predictive-density envelope.

results.claim: For the current r82/r84 reference-good events and Gaussian KL>=1 alternatives with variance ratio r in [0.065,3.4], the power-relevant standardized separation of a positive mean alternative from the worst reference interval endpoint is theta(r)=[sqrt(3+log r-r)-a]/sqrt(r), where a=2*z_0.995*cU/sqrt(684)=0.2264702713 in baseline-sigma units. KL>1 only increases theta at fixed r. On the KL=1 shell, theta has at most one interior critical point and it is a maximum: theta'(r) has the sign of a-(2+log r)/sqrt(3+log r-r); for r>exp(-2), g(r)=(2+log r)/sqrt(3+log r-r) is increasing because g'(r) has numerator 4+(1+r)log r>0 on the relevant interval, while for r<=exp(-2) theta'>0. Therefore the minimum is at an endpoint. Numerically theta(0.065)=0.87297 and theta(3.4)=0.3694057, so the exact worst moderate direction is r=3.4, not the old rectangle combination of minimum mean shift at r=0.065 with maximum variance at r=3.4.
results.impact: This removes the main conservatism in the r82 mean-delay proof without a continuum Monte Carlo over r. The lower-surrogate CI-inf t factor for the correct sign is samplewise nondecreasing in theta, so theta*=0.3694057 is a uniform worst-direction reduction for the moderate Gaussian KL>=1 branch.

results.claim: For m=32,c=2.7 and theta*=0.3694057, write the one-sided lower-surrogate block factor as log E = 0.5 log(c^2/(m+c^2)) + (m/2)[log(W+m d^2)-log(W+b d^2)], b=m c^2/(m+c^2), d=max(theta*+Z/sqrt(m),0), Z~N(0,1), W~chi2_{31} independent. Hence for n clean post blocks and component threshold B, P(sum log E < B) <= exp(lambda B+n log E[exp(-lambda log E)]) for every lambda>0. Deterministic Gauss-Hermite x generalized-Gauss-Laguerre quadrature gave mean block log-growth about 1.20053 nat; quadrature orders 40,60,80,100,140 agreed to a few 1e-5 in the mean but are not interval certified.
results.comparison: Against the r82 rectangle-normal proof, the corresponding retained mean-channel 95% raw bounds were 1152 at start, 1656 after 1000, and 2400 after 1e6; the new sufficient bounds are about 2.1x shorter at those matched points. This is a deterministic-numerical Chernoff calculation, not a directed-rounding theorem.

results.claim: A more general common-increment factor can be formed without choosing a direction. Freeze any reference-measurable Gaussian null confidence set C_R and any proper reference-measurable joint predictive density q_R(y_1:m). Define E_UI(Y;R)=q_R(Y)/sup_{theta in C_R} p_theta^m(Y). On the reference-good event theta0 in C_R, E_UI <= q_R/p_theta0 pointwise, so E_theta0[E_UI|R]<=1. Reusing the same frozen q_R and C_R over deterministic nonoverlapping future blocks therefore gives conditional e-values, and because every delayed start sees the same current-block multiplier, the exact r82 telescoping heavy-tail start-mixture recursion remains O(1) state.
results.gaussian_closed_form: For C_R=[M_L,M_U]x[L,U], the denominator is exact from block sufficient statistics: mu_hat=projection(ybar,[M_L,M_U]), S=W+m(ybar-mu_hat)^2, sigma_hat=clip(sqrt(S/m),[L,U]), log sup p=-m/2 log(2pi)-m log sigma_hat-S/(2 sigma_hat^2). A proper Normal-Inverse-Gamma predictive numerator with m0=Xbar_R, kappa0=3, alpha0=3, beta0=2*s_R^2 has log q=-m/2 log(2pi)+0.5 log(kappa0/(kappa0+m))+alpha0 log beta0-alpha_n log beta_n+logGamma(alpha_n)-logGamma(alpha0), alpha_n=alpha0+m/2, beta_n=beta0+W/2+kappa0*m(ybar-m0)^2/[2(kappa0+m)].
results.typeI_scope: Exact conditional e-validity on the current r82 reference confidence event; the existing 0.02 reference-failure union plus conditional e-process budget can be retained. No numerical power calculation is needed for type-I validity.

results.claim: The NIG envelope above was tuned only on a discovery Monte Carlo grid over the exact Gaussian KL=1 shell. A separate deterministic quadrature stress then scanned variance ratio across the full exact-KL=1 shell, reference variance statistic across its [q_0.005,q_0.995] good-event range, and reference-mean error across its full good-event interval. The worst scanned expected log growth remained about 12.04 nat per 32-sample block, with the weakest region near r about 2.7-3.5 and the widest/high-side reference set. Conditional-null quadrature over the same reference-good grid had E[E_UI] at most about 0.401, consistent with but much more conservative than the analytic <=1 guarantee.
results.hybrid_candidate: Keep the two specialized r82 variance channels at weight 0.25 each and replace the two mean channels by one universal envelope at weight 0.50. This preserves the current fast variance-down/up specialization while using one omnibus factor for the moderate branch.
results.numerical_method: 32x32 Gaussian/chi-square quadrature with inner Chernoff-lambda minimization and differential-evolution search over exact-KL=1 variance ratio plus the continuous reference-good variance/mean-error envelope. A denser fixed grid gave consistent worst regions. These are strong engineering/deterministic-numerical results, not interval-certified global optimization.

negative_or_scope_evidence: The r85b Chernoff constants use high-order deterministic quadrature but not directed-rounding special-function or quadrature enclosures; retain the symbolic Chernoff formula as authoritative and decimals as non-machine-certified.

The universal-envelope type-I proof is exact on the frozen confidence-set good event, but the power stress is not yet a continuum theorem. Differential evolution and dense grids do not certify a global maximum of the miss bound.
The NIG hyperparameters kappa0=3,alpha0=3 were selected on a discovery grid. They must not be described as minimax optimal.

A single universal envelope is slower than the existing specialized variance-down channel on some pure-variance cases, so r85 does not support deleting the specialized variance channels. The current best candidate is a 0.25/0.25/0.50 variance-up/variance-down/universal hybrid.
All claims remain within a clean iid Gaussian reference followed by one fixed iid Gaussian step law. No heavy-tail, serial-dependence, gradual-drift or repeated-change guarantee follows.
The exact-KL=1 power scan does not by itself prove monotonic improvement for every KL>1 alternative under the universal envelope, even though the likelihood geometry suggests stronger separation.
frontier: Turn the r85d universal-envelope power stress into a continuum certificate. First reduce the reference-good envelope analytically if possible (the numerical worst is consistently widest variance CI and mean error toward the alternative); then certify the remaining Gaussian KL=1 radial/directional domain with interval arithmetic or discovery/independent-validation KL transport.
Prove or refute radial monotonicity of the universal-envelope miss Chernoff bound for KL>=1. If monotonicity fails, cover a finite outer shell and derive an analytic high-KL handoff.

Run a matched common-random detector comparison of the existing r82 four-direction guard, the r84 CI-inf-t replacement, and the r85 0.25/0.25/0.50 hybrid at identical total PFA=0.05, including immediate, 1k, 10k, 100k and 1e6 changepoints and pure-variance endpoints.

Try RIPr/numeraire or a better proper predictive numerator only after the r85 NIG envelope is continuum-certified; the null quadrature mean around <=0.401 shows potentially large conservatism but optimizing it before certification risks churn.

Replace Gaussian/chi-square quadrature and confidence-limit decimal constants with true directed-rounding interval enclosures if available; otherwise preserve symbolic formulas and mark numeric power bounds non-machine-certified.
exact_next_action: Keep the r85 NIG universal factor frozen at kappa0=3,alpha0=3,beta0=2*s_R^2 and hybrid weights {variance_up:0.25,variance_down:0.25,universal:0.50}. Derive analytic monotonicity in reference mean-error and reference variance-statistic if possible, then continuum-certify the exact Gaussian KL=1 miss-Chernoff surface under that worst reference envelope. In parallel run matched common-random late-change simulations against r82 and r84 without retuning. Promote only if both the exact conditional type-I proof and a continuum/matched-power result survive; otherwise retain r84 as the safer mean-channel improvement.
